land.text: the Papal States left after the cessions of 1797: 'territory conquered from the Papal States', with the Tiberina and Anconine Republics incorporated

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's own Papal States row draws this land for 1797..1798 and then has no shape in 1799, when this row stands in; the two rows cover the same cells.

successors.note: 30 September 1799: the second Neapolitan invasion occupies the Republic (infobox 'Neapolitan occupation: 30 September 1799'); the occupation lasts until the Papal restoration. The slug is Cliopatria's row for the Bourbon kingdom of Naples (1762..1814).
'the Papal States were restored under the rule of Pope Pius VII in June 1800'.

correction.text: New keyframe: the shape of 1799 applied to 1798 (15 February 1798 onward): the republic 'comprised territory conquered from the Papal States' and incorporated the Tiberina and Anconine Republics

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria has no shape for this row in 1798; it files the same land under its Papal States row (111 cells, 1797..1798) and gives this row only 1799 (114 cells). The page names no provinces and no area, so the cell sets are compared with each other, not with the page.

30,084 km2: Lazio, Umbria and the Marche (Perugia 20, Rome 18, Macerata 13, Viterbo 12, Frosinone 10, Latina 8, Terni 7, Rieti 7, Ascoli Piceno 5, Ancona 5, Pesaro e Urbino 4, a Fermo cell, and two L'Aquila and two Caserta edge cells). The page gives no area and names no province, so the shape stands as unverified in detail. It is right only until 30 September 1799; the Neapolitan occupation that follows is the successors' (Cliopatria has no shape for it).

region.text: the Papal States rump: Lazio, Umbria and the Marche, with the Tiberina and Anconine Republics incorporated

ledger.note: 15 February 1798: Berthier proclaims the Roman Republic at Rome. 'Berthier proclaimed the Roman Republic on 15 February 1798' after French troops 'invaded the Papal States and occupied Rome on 11 February 1798'; Pius VI was 'escorted out of Rome on 20 February and exiled to France'. Infobox status 'Sister republic of Revolutionary France'. The page names the land only as 'territory conquered from the Papal States'.

region.text: Rome and Latium, the zone the page implies by the French re-entry into Rome

ledger.note: November 1798: Naples invades. 'The Kingdom of Naples invaded the Roman Republic in November 1798.' The page does not say which land the Neapolitans took; it says the French 're-entered Rome on 14 December 1798', so Rome and its surroundings are the zone.
14 December 1798: the French re-enter Rome. 'The French re-entered Rome on 14 December 1798, after defeating the Neapolitans at several battles'; Championnet then took Naples in January 1799.

30 September 1799: the Republic falls to Naples. 'Following a second Neapolitan invasion on 30 September 1799, the Papal States were restored under the rule of Pope Pius VII in June 1800'; infobox 'Neapolitan occupation: 30 September 1799'. The page puts the end with the Papal restoration of June 1800; the occupation is the end of the Republic's own government.
30 September 1799: the Roman Republic ends under Neapolitan occupation; the land reverts to the Papal States in June 1800.

wars.name: Neapolitan invasion of the Roman Republic (1798)
wars.outcome: The Neapolitans invaded in November 1798; the French defeated them in several battles and re-entered Rome on 14 December 1798; Championnet occupied Naples in January 1799 and proclaimed the Parthenopean Republic.
wars.note: The page names no battle and no territory held by Naples; the zone is an inference.

wars.name: Second Neapolitan invasion of the Roman Republic (1799)
wars.outcome: The invasion of 30 September 1799 ended the Republic; the Papal States were restored under Pius VII in June 1800.
wars.note: The Directory dossier (french-directory) records the collapse of the sister republics after Novi (15 August 1799); this page dates the Neapolitan occupation, not Novi.

certainty.note: The page gives no boundary; the frontier with Naples was fought over in November-December 1798, and the Republic's land is drawn from the old Papal States.

sources.title: Roman Republic (1798-1799)
sources.note: Identity, proclamation 15 February 1798, French entry 11 February, Neapolitan invasions of November 1798 and 30 September 1799, Papal restoration of June 1800; no area and no provinces.

notes: Different state from roman-republic: Cliopatria's Revolutionary Roman Republic carries Wikidata Q175881, which is the ancient Roman Republic's id (it shares it with the roman-republic row, -500..-32); this is the 1798-1799 sister republic. Two states, two dossiers; the wikidata field keeps Cliopatria's value, and the site should not link it to the ancient Republic's item. Cliopatria's life for this row is 1799 only; the Republic was proclaimed on 15 February 1798, so a 1798 keyframe is added, and Cliopatria's Papal States row (1797..1798) draws the same cells for those years (the papal-states dossier, eu-13, should end its shape 1797..1798 at the proclamation of 15 February 1798 and restart in June 1800; Cliopatria draws no Papal States shape for 1799 and then 148 cells for 1800..1802). Undated on the page: the Tiberina and Anconine Republics incorporated into the Republic; they need dossiers if the gazetteer agents want them. The Directory dossier dates the proclamation 10 February 1798; this page says the French entered Rome on 11 February and the proclamation was on 15 February. San Marino neighbours the Republic in 1799 (Cliopatria seed) and stayed independent. No infobox area; page budget 1 page of 1-2.
